reviewer: Independent source reviewer t3_reviewer_b; one dossier
reason: The complete original supports three distinct continuing leave-transfer rules and their shared retroactive activation. The complete revoker expressly ends the order effective February 15, 1981. The candidate correctly declines to equate that formal revocation with the earliest cessation of rules grounded in specifically incorporated 1946 statutory provisions. Concrete 1951 leave-law and 1980 transition sources leave statutory displacement, savings and accrued balances unresolved. All three first ends, whole-order end, savings and final later-search closure remain withheld. The related sources do not contradict those limited findings.

inventory_assessment.paragraph_1: Persons within sections 934(b)/935 who elect to transfer annual leave must transfer all accumulated and current accrued leave up to the receiving agency maximum at entrance.
inventory_assessment.paragraph_2: For the specified statutory transfers, five work-days equal seven calendar days.
inventory_assessment.paragraph_3: Construes the section 935 annual/sick-leave ceiling to include current accrual as well as accumulation.
inventory_assessment.preamble: Defines covered Reserve assignments and subsequent reinstatement, and resignations followed by appointments between Foreign Service and other agencies; retained verbatim and limits all three rules.
inventory_assessment.paragraph_4: Common activation provision is attached to each unit; it is not a separately continuing duty.
inventory_assessment.excluded_neighbors: Agricultural milk rule, contents, title and signature are not additional operative units.

accepted_scope.activation_basis: Original paragraph 4, expressly effective as of that date; signature March 27, 1947 is not substituted.
accepted_scope.own_terms: No sunset, reporting deadline, completion trigger or evidence of spent execution. These are recurring rules for qualifying transfers.
accepted_scope.revocation_basis: EO12292 sections 10(c) and 11, rather than February 23 signature or February 25 publication.
accepted_scope.limitation: Formal withdrawal of the original directives is supported. This does not establish that accrued leave, completed transfers or independently preserved statutory effects disappeared.

related_source_findings.EO9932: Complete status/reinstatement order. Section 528 return-to-duty rights and implementing regulations are distinct from sections 934(b)/935 leave balance calculation; no target repeal is stated.
related_source_findings.EO10471: Complete order authorizes leave under 1951 Act section 202(c)(2) for chief-of-mission compensation recipients, effective July 5, 1953. Concrete later-law scope lead, not a dated end of all target rules.
related_source_findings.EO10477_and_EO10522: Complete administrative/personnel authority instruments read. USIA authority, statutory compliance and Board-function allocation do not themselves terminate the three original rules.
related_source_findings.EO10540: Complete order and attached schedule read. Excludes specified officers from the 1951 Act and delegates designation; paragraph 1 follows a first-pay-period condition. No universal target ending inferred from that condition.
related_source_findings.EO10893: Prior complete reading retained; sections 302-306 reread. Foreign-assistance personnel and section 528 benefits are separately sourced. Savings are bounded to functions affected by that order.
related_source_findings.EO10903: Complete actual order read. Allowances/differentials/benefits and specific leave delegation are distinct; its revocation list does not name EO9837. Section 5(b) has a garbled OCR ending, which is not used to decide the unresolved target savings issue.
related_source_findings.EO11034_and_EO11228: Complete orders read, including supersession and savings. Exchange-program benefits and 1951 section 203(f) leave authority are distinct functions; their bounded savings do not prove continuation of EO9837 after formal revocation.
related_source_findings.CSC_Part30_1963: The actual actor is the Civil Service Commission regulation on 28 FR 2023, PDF page 5 in the EO11096 container. Complete amendment read. Its 90-day qualifying rule addresses transfers from another leave system and accrual, effective March 17, 1963. It is a concrete leave-law lead, not an EO11096 amendment or proof of the original rules’ earliest end.
related_source_findings.EO12589: Complete 1987 donation-program order read. Transfers of leave between employees for emergencies are distinct from transferring one employee’s balance between systems; no revival of EO9837.
related_source_findings.EO12293: Complete new 1980 Act administration order reread. Section 5 expressly invokes sections 2101/2107 for pay and benefits pending conversion. It establishes a concrete statutory-transition investigation, not a finding that all target rules survived or were revived.
related_source_findings.additional_EO11579: Complete independently located OPIC order read. Separate compensation and personnel-restoration authority with function-bounded savings; no target ending or revival. No unverified bylaw-adoption date inferred.

statutory_gap_assessment.1980: Actual transition and repeal/savings terms remain unread; no accrued-leave cancellation or automatic EO continuity is inferred.
statutory_gap_assessment.effect: Supports honest partial acceptance, not complete readiness.

unresolved_material_gaps.gap: The operative Annual and Sick Leave Act of 1951 provisions on coverage, accrual, inter-system transfer, repeal of the 1946 Foreign Service leave provisions, effective date and savings are not held in the located source set. Official later texts establish that Act as the applicable leave-law framework and the 1963 Part 30 amendment regulates transfers between leave systems, but neither establishes whether/when each original EO9837 rule first ceased. Resolve the original statutory authorities, any repeal or replacement, and accrued-leave treatment before assigning first-end dates.
